claims.title: Aboriginal peoples settle the continent
claims.summary: Aboriginal peoples reached Australia at least 65,000 years ago, crossing from Southeast Asia to the joined landmass of Sahul and beginning the world's oldest continuous human occupation of a single territory.

sources.label: Defining Moments: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander history

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-65000bce-aboriginal-peoples-settle-the-continent, claim TL:AUS:event:65000bce:aboriginal-peoples-settle-the-continent, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Settlement across the whole continent
claims.summary: Within tens of thousands of years, Aboriginal peoples had spread across the entire continent, from tropical north to the cold south, developing diverse cultures adapted to every environment.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-50000bce-settlement-across-the-whole-continent, claim TL:AUS:event:50000bce:settlement-across-the-whole-continent, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hundreds of nations and languages
claims.summary: By the time of European contact the continent was home to hundreds of distinct nations speaking around 250 languages, sustaining complex law, kinship, trade, art, and spiritual systems centred on connection to Country.

sources.label: Defining Moments: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander history

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1500bce-hundreds-of-nations-and-languages, claim TL:AUS:event:1500bce:hundreds-of-nations-and-languages, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cook charts and claims the east coast
claims.summary: Lieutenant James Cook charted the eastern coast of the continent aboard HMB Endeavour and claimed it for Britain as New South Wales, opening the way to British colonisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1770-cook-charts-and-claims-the-east-coast, claim TL:AUS:event:1770:cook-charts-and-claims-the-east-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The First Fleet founds the penal colony
claims.summary: Captain Arthur Phillip's First Fleet established a British penal colony at Sydney Cove, beginning permanent European settlement and the dispossession of Aboriginal peoples of the Sydney region.

sources.label: Defining Moments: Convict cargo and the First Fleet

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1788-the-first-fleet-founds-the-penal-colony, claim TL:AUS:event:1788:the-first-fleet-founds-the-penal-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Smallpox devastates Aboriginal peoples
claims.summary: A smallpox epidemic spread among Aboriginal peoples around Sydney, killing a large proportion of the Eora and neighbouring peoples and compounding the impact of land seizure and conflict.

sources.label: Defining Moments: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander history

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1789-smallpox-devastates-aboriginal-peoples, claim TL:AUS:event:1789:smallpox-devastates-aboriginal-peoples, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The frontier wars
claims.summary: Across the continent, the expansion of pastoral settlement met Aboriginal resistance in a long, dispersed frontier conflict of raids, reprisals, and massacres that, with introduced disease, devastated Aboriginal peoples and dispossessed them of their land.

sources.label: Defining Moments: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander history

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1824-the-frontier-wars, claim TL:AUS:event:1824:the-frontier-wars, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gold rushes begin
claims.summary: Discoveries of gold in New South Wales and Victoria triggered rushes that drew hundreds of thousands of migrants, transforming the colonies' population, economy, and society within a decade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1851-gold-rushes-begin, claim TL:AUS:event:1851:gold-rushes-begin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Eureka Stockade
claims.summary: Goldminers at Ballarat rebelled against oppressive licensing and the denial of political rights; troops stormed their stockade, killing more than twenty, but the revolt helped secure democratic reforms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1854-eureka-stockade, claim TL:AUS:event:1854:eureka-stockade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Federation creates the Commonwealth of Australia
claims.summary: Six self-governing colonies federated under a written Constitution to form the Commonwealth of Australia, a new federal nation with a parliament in which power was shared between the Commonwealth and the states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1901-federation-creates-the-commonwealth-of-australia, claim TL:AUS:event:1901:federation-creates-the-commonwealth-of-australia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Immigration Restriction Act and 'White Australia'
claims.summary: One of the new parliament's first laws established the cornerstone of the 'White Australia' policy, using a dictation test to exclude non-European migrants and keep the nation overwhelmingly white and British.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1901-immigration-restriction-act-and-white-australia, claim TL:AUS:event:1901:immigration-restriction-act-and-white-australia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Women win the federal vote
claims.summary: The Commonwealth Franchise Act gave most (non-Aboriginal) women the right to vote and to stand for the federal parliament, making Australia one of the first nations to enfranchise women nationally.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1902-women-win-the-federal-vote, claim TL:AUS:event:1902:women-win-the-federal-vote, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gallipoli landing and the Anzac legend
claims.summary: Australian and New Zealand troops landed at Gallipoli in a costly campaign that, despite ending in withdrawal, became a foundational national story commemorated each year on Anzac Day.

sources.label: The Immigration Restriction Act and the Anzacs

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1915-gallipoli-landing-and-the-anzac-legend, claim TL:AUS:event:1915:gallipoli-landing-and-the-anzac-legend, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Stolen Generations
claims.summary: Under official assimilation policies, governments and churches forcibly removed many thousands of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families over decades, causing profound and lasting harm.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1910-the-stolen-generations, claim TL:AUS:event:1910:the-stolen-generations, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bombing of Darwin
claims.summary: Japanese aircraft bombed Darwin during the Second World War, the largest attack ever mounted on Australia, prompting Australia to turn increasingly toward the United States for security.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1942-bombing-of-darwin, claim TL:AUS:event:1942:bombing-of-darwin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Post-war mass immigration
claims.summary: A large post-war immigration programme brought millions of migrants, first from Europe and later from Asia and beyond, transforming Australia into a far more diverse society.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1945-post-war-mass-immigration, claim TL:AUS:event:1945:post-war-mass-immigration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 1967 referendum
claims.summary: Australians voted by nearly 91 per cent to let the Commonwealth make laws for Aboriginal people and to include them in the census, a landmark in the struggle for Aboriginal rights and recognition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1967-the-1967-referendum, claim TL:AUS:event:1967:the-1967-referendum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Australia Act and full legal independence
claims.summary: The Australia Act 1986, building on the Statute of Westminster adopted in 1942, ended the British Parliament's power to legislate for Australia and abolished appeals to the Privy Council, completing Australia's legal independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1986-australia-act-and-full-legal-independence, claim TL:AUS:event:1986:australia-act-and-full-legal-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mabo decision overturns terra nullius
claims.summary: The High Court ruled in Mabo v Queensland that the continent had not been terra nullius and that Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples could hold native title, leading to the Native Title Act 1993.

sources.label: The Mabo Case
sources.publisher: Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies (AIATSIS)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-1992-mabo-decision-overturns-terra-nullius, claim TL:AUS:event:1992:mabo-decision-overturns-terra-nullius, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: National Apology to the Stolen Generations
claims.summary: Prime Minister Kevin Rudd delivered a formal apology in parliament to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and especially to the Stolen Generations harmed by past policies of forced child removal.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-2008-national-apology-to-the-stolen-generations, claim TL:AUS:event:2008:national-apology-to-the-stolen-generations, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Voice to Parliament referendum
claims.summary: Australians voted against a constitutional amendment to recognise First Peoples and establish an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Voice to Parliament, leaving questions of recognition and reconciliation unresolved.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Australia: From the world's oldest continuous cultures and a British penal colony to a federated, multicultural democracy.", terralore.co/country/AUS/chronicle#ev-2023-voice-to-parliament-referendum, claim TL:AUS:event:2023:voice-to-parliament-referendum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
